chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Muawiya ibn Ammar and Hafs ibn Al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

It is befitting for the pilgrim, when he has completed his rituals and intends to depart, to buy dates with a dirham to give in charity, so that it serves as an expiation for whatever may have entered upon him during his Hajj, such as scratching or lice falling off, or similar to that.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended charity for a pilgrim to give after completing Hajj rituals?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this act serves as a precautionary expiation (kaffarah) for minor ritual impurities or distractions, such as scratching or lice, which might have invalidated parts of the Hajj. The specific instruction to purchase dates with a dirham highlights the emphasis on accessible, everyday charity as a means of spiritual purification before departing Mecca. This practice reflects the scholarly view that while Hajj is valid, seeking perfection through such recommended acts ensures the completeness of the pilgrimage's reward.
